newsitem.title: USA: BG&E, Potomac say merger cannot proceed.
newsitem.headline: BG&E, Potomac say merger cannot proceed.

text.p: Baltimore Gas and Electric Co and Potomac Electric Power Co (PEPCO) filed sworn affidavits in Baltimore County Circuit Court Monday stating they cannot merge their companies even if an $8.5 million computational error in the Maryland Public Service Commission's April 16 order approving the merger was fixed.
The companies did not disclose the nature of the error, and company officials were unavailable for further comment.
The companies asked the court to send the merger case back to the Maryland Public Service Commission for reconsideration.

They added that although the commission approved the merger, "it attached conditions that would not provide adequate, if any benefits, to shareholders," and that the error "does not provide an adequate financial basis upon which BGE and PEPCO could proceed to consummate the merger."

The companies have asked for a rehearing of the original order, but said that Local 1900 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers appealed the order to the Circuit Court. They said in their affidavit that "the only purpose to this appeal is to give meaning to the IBEW's strategy of delay in the hope that the merger will not be consummated."
